slides.title: What is an Enum?
slides.content: An enum (enumeration) is a distinct value type consisting of a set of named constants. It improves code readability by replacing magic numbers.
slides.example: public enum Day { Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday }

exercise.prompt: What is the primary benefit of using enums?
options: Replacing magic numbers with named constants
exercise.answer: Replacing magic numbers with named constants

slides.title: Declaring Enums
slides.content: Declare enums with the 'enum' keyword inside a namespace or class. By default, the first value is 0 and increments by 1.

exercise.prompt: Complete: public _____ Priority { Low, Medium, High }

slides.title: Underlying Types
slides.content: You can specify an underlying integral type after a colon: byte, short, int, long, etc. The default is int.
slides.example: public enum SmallStatus : byte { Off = 0, On = 1 }

exercise.prompt: Complete the enum declaration with the correct underlying type.

slides.title: Casting Enums
slides.content: Cast between enums and their underlying numeric types using standard C# casting syntax.

exercise.prompt: Cast the Color enum value Blue to its underlying integer and print it.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: Parse, Cast
When run, your code should output: 3

slides.title: Enum.Parse and Enum.TryParse
slides.content: Enum.Parse converts a string to an enum value. Enum.TryParse is safer, returning a bool indicating success.

exercise.prompt: Which method safely parses a string to an enum without throwing?

slides.title: Iterating Over Enums
slides.content: Use Enum.GetValues() to iterate over all defined enum constants at runtime.

slides.title: Flags Enums
slides.content: Mark an enum with [Flags] to treat values as bit fields, allowing combination of values using bitwise operators.

exercise.prompt: Match the Flags enum values to their binary representations.

slides.title: Enum Best Practices
slides.content: Use enums for fixed sets of related constants. Avoid using enum values as strings directly; use ToString() for display and descriptions for user-friendly text.

exercise.prompt: Use a switch expression to convert Status.Rejected to the string "Denied" and print it.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: switch
When run, your code should output: Denied
